It makes the device's reviewed language key ('erp.language', kept across sign-out by design) also hold the record address on which the language was last switched, and the shell opens that address after the next sign-in. biggest_gap.title: The browser tenant-isolation gate never uses the shell's own language switch, so a device-kept key that carries one tenant's record to the next person's tab passes every check
biggest_gap.detail: The shell keeps a few keys on the device across sign-out by design: the language ('erp.language') and the digits. G1 judges them two ways. The static G1ClientState gate counts carrier uses and module-level state. The browser journey in tests/e2e/specs/client-isolation.spec.ts takes tenant B through every menu screen, the palette, a record and the dialogs, then judges A's tab. But that journey never presses Alt+L, the top-bar language button or the digits switch while B's data is on screen. Nothing therefore checks what a reviewed device key holds after the shell's main action has run. I planted CL3b: the existing getItem and setItem of 'erp.language' also carry the record address the language was switched on, and after the next sign-in the shell opens it. It adds no new storage call and no module-level state. It passed the web unit suite (537 of 537), G1ClientStateTests and the whole e2e suite, the client-isolation spec included. At run time it is a real cross-tenant leak: Gulf Steel's admin, signing in on the tab Al Noor's admin left, is put on Al Noor's user record address with Al Noor's e-mail in the search box. Under the round rules, a gate that misses a fault planted in this piece's surface fails the round. On a shared shop-floor or front-desk PC at a UAE trading company, this is exactly how one company's customer or staff details would show up in another's session. Fix: in the browser G1 journey, have B switch language and digits (Alt+L, the digits action, My account) while one of B's records is open, before signing out. Judge every device-kept key's value against B's markers after sign-out and on A's every step, as localStorage already is. Add a value check for the device keys: 'erp.language' may hold only en or ar, and 'erp.numerals' only latn or arab, so anything else fails. Add CL3b as a self-test plant.
